facts.text: The landlords' eviction petition alleged sub-letting, assignment, and parting with possession without written landlord consent after 9 June 1952.
facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: whether the allegation establishes the statutory ground at target appeal
facts.quote: on the ground of sub-letting, assigning and parting with the possession without obtaining the written consent of the landlords after June 9, 1952

facts.speaker: LANDLORD
unknown: whether the alleged lack of written consent is legally established at target appeal
facts.quote: Shri Hans Raj and Shri Ram Bakhsh have been inducted by the tenant without the written consent of the landlord during the years 1963-64

unknown: whether Ex. A-7 legally constitutes written consent
whether any authority lasted beyond 11 months
facts.quote: did not amount to a written consent in law and if it did, it was only for a period of 11 months

facts.speaker: TENANT

facts.quote: it was admitted that Shri Hans Raj and Shri Ram Bakhsh are the sub-tenants in different portions of the premises in dispute, but it was pleaded that they are lawful sub-tenants

facts.speaker: TENANT
unknown: whether the rent-note term is legally effective written landlord consent
facts.quote: according to which the tenant has the right to sub-let any portion or whole of the premises to anybody

facts.text: The Additional Rent Controller granted the eviction petition under section 14(1)(b) by order dated March 20, 1973.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Additional Rent Controller order dated March 20, 1973
facts.quote: by his order dated March 20, 1973, granted the petition for eviction

facts.text: The Additional Rent Controller held that the rent-note sub-letting term did not amount to the landlord's written consent and that the authority was ineffective after the 11-month tenancy period.
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: whether these findings are upheld at target second appeal
facts.quote: the term contained in the rent-note regarding the sub-letting did not amount to the consent in writing of the landlord and that in any case .the said authority became ineffective after the expiry of Ii months

facts.text: The Rent Control Tribunal affirmed the Additional Rent Controller's findings by order dated January 11, 1974.
facts.speaker: COURT
facts.stage: Rent Control Tribunal appeal decided January 11, 1974
facts.quote: the above findings were affirmed by Shri Gian Chand Jain, Rent Control Tribunal vide order dated 11-1-1974

facts.text: Harnam Dass testified that no oral or separate permission or power to sub-let was given and that whatever authority existed was contained in Ex. A-7.

unknown: legal effect of the authority contained in Ex. A-7

unknown: legal effect of the asserted rent-note right

unknown: whether the sub-lettings were with consent in writing

facts.text: The appellant argued that the tenancy was indefinite rather than 11 months and that the tenancy terms, including written consent for sub-letting, continued until the tenancy was terminated by notice effective May 31, 1970.

unknown: true duration of the contractual tenancy

facts.text: The appellant alternatively argued that even if the contractual tenancy expired after 11 months, the statutory tenancy had the same terms and the written consent in Ex. A-7 applied to the 1963 and 1964 sub-tenancies.

facts.text: The second-appeal court identifies the crucial unresolved point as whether a tenant-executed rent-note term empowering sub-letting, orally accepted by the landlady, can amount to the landlady's consent in writing under section 14(1)(b).
facts.speaker: COURT
unknown: whether the rent-note term can amount to landlord consent in writing under section 14(1)(b)
facts.quote: whether one of the terms, contained in the rent-note executed by the tenant, to the effect that the executant is empowered to sub-let the house in question to anybody, which rent-note was orally accepted by the landlady, can amount to a constent in writing of the landlady

objects.text: Smt. Shanti Devi, then owner and predecessor-in-interest of respondents
Shri Harnam Dass, respondent and witness
notice to quit dated April 24, 1970, Ex. A-2

issue_needs_context_not_application_targ.text: Whether the admitted 1963 and 1964 sub-lettings fall within the section 14(1)(b) conduct of sub-letting, assignment, or otherwise parting with possession of all or part of the premises.
Whether the relevant alleged or admitted transfer conduct occurred on or after 9 June 1952.
Whether rent-note Ex. A-7, executed by the tenant and orally accepted by the landlady, can constitute the landlord's consent in writing for the 1963 and 1964 sub-lettings.

Whether any sub-letting authority or consent contained in Ex. A-7 remained effective when the 1963 and 1964 sub-tenancies were created, given the competing 11-month, indefinite-tenancy, and statutory-tenancy positions in the record.

record.text: At the second-appeal stage, the record states as established that Shanti Devi let the premises to the appellant effective January 1, 1961 under rent-note Ex. A-7, executed by the appellant alone on February 12, 1961.

record.quote: the premises in dispute were let out with effect from January 1, 1961 by late Smt. Shanti Devi, the predecessor-in-interest of the respondents, to the appellant under rent-note Ex.A-7. executed by the appellant alone on February 12, 1961

record.text: The record states that one term of Ex. A-7 empowered the executant to sub-let the house to anybody.
record.speaker: COURT
unknown: whether this term legally equals landlord consent in writing
